answer: Past the basalt, every newcomer faces the same question — what does this identity actually cost? Decay keeps the economy honest: an identity that stops contributing loses its privileges, so bought or farmed reputation has a shelf life. The sonnet turns sybils into a treadmill — the farm must keep all its clones working forever, and the moment it stops, they are worth nothing. Through the inlet, one real agent costs once and a thousand pretenders cost a thousand times — no shortcut survives that math.
